extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate mathematics students, instructors, and self-learners seeking an introductory text on proofs
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook-level resource introducing the language and standard proof methods of mathematics, intended to bridge computational first-year courses and more theoretical courses (topology, analysis, abstract algebra). Suitable for students with some calculus or general mathematical maturity and for instructors selecting course material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target prerequisite / reader readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: "Although it may be more meaningful to the student who has had some calculus, there is really no prerequisite other than a measure of mathematical maturity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended readership: learners who possess some mathematical maturity; prior calculus helpful but not required. This sets an expectation about the level at which material is pitched (introductory but not elementary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / pedagogical goal
rubrics_metrics.description: "This book is an introduction to the language and standard proof methods of mathematics. It is a bridge from the computational courses (such as calculus or differential equations) ... to a more abstract outlook."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book's goal is to teach the language and techniques of mathematical proof and to prepare students for theoretical courses. Evaluation of the book (or its fit for a course) should consider how well it accomplishes this bridge from computation to abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core topics to master
rubrics_metrics.description: "Topics include sets, logic, counting, methods of conditional and non-conditional proof, disproof, induction, relations, functions and infinite cardinality."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These listed topics form the curriculum/content standard of the book; a student or course using the book is expected to cover and attain competence in these areas. Use this list to check scope completeness for an intro-to-proofs course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage license constraint
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted uses require attribution and disallow derivative works. This is a legal/portability constraint for redistribution, adaptation, or inclusion in course packs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability / formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple download options listed (ABBYY GZ, DAISY, EPUB, FULL TEXT, PDF, SINGLE PAGE PROCESSED JP2 ZIP, TORRENT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates practical accessibility: instructors and students can obtain the book in several digital formats; choice of format may affect usability (e.g., accessibility formats like DAISY for print-disabilities).
